title: AWS Certified Solutions Architect – Associate (SAA-C03) High-Availability & Disaster Recovery Architecture
problem: Software engineers and architects preparing for the AWS Solutions Architect – Associate (SAA-C03) certification frequently memorize theoretical architecture diagrams and high-level service definitions without ever constructing a resilient, multi-AZ cloud architecture from code. When faced with production system designs, they struggle to implement automated multi-AZ load balancer failovers, configure asynchronous SQS decoupling, enforce KMS envelope encryption, or automate S3 lifecycle archival policies. This guide delivers a rigorous hands-on lab curriculum and reproducible architecture implementation in Terraform and LocalStack/AWS. The engineer architects an Application Load Balancer across multi-AZ subnets, implements an auto-scaling compute tier, decouples message processing via Amazon SQS, secures data with AWS KMS envelope encryption, automates S3 lifecycle tiering, and verifies 99.9% uptime during simulated availability zone outages.

use_cases.title: Multi-AZ High-Availability Web Application Resiliency
use_cases.first_sentence: Enterprise customer portals requiring 99.99% operational availability must survive sudden hardware failures or complete availability zone data center blackouts.
use_cases.second_sentence: The architecture deploys redundant compute instances across multiple availability zones behind an Application Load Balancer, executing sub-5s automatic failover routing.

use_cases.title: Asynchronous Decoupled Message Processing with Amazon SQS
use_cases.first_sentence: E-commerce order intake services experience extreme traffic spikes during promotional flash sales that threaten to overwhelm downstream billing databases.
use_cases.second_sentence: The system buffers incoming orders in an Amazon SQS distributed queue, allowing background worker pools to consume messages at a sustainable processing rate.

use_cases.title: Automated S3 Storage Cost Optimization & KMS Envelope Encryption
use_cases.first_sentence: Healthcare compliance architectures storing petabytes of patient audit logs must enforce cryptographic encryption at rest while minimizing storage costs.
use_cases.second_sentence: The pipeline encrypts object payloads with customer-managed AWS KMS keys and schedules lifecycle policies that transition inactive data to S3 Glacier after 30 days.

hard_parts: Architecting resilient multi-AZ network topologies with private subnet NAT gateways and resilient ALB target group health checks
Implementing automated worker auto-scaling policies driven by Amazon SQS queue depth metrics (`ApproximateNumberOfMessagesVisible`)
Configuring AWS KMS envelope encryption with customer managed keys (CMK) and key rotation policies across object storage
Simulating availability zone failure scenarios and verifying zero dropped connections and automated health check recovery
screener_signals: Clean Terraform infrastructure repository cleanly defining multi-AZ VPC, ALB target groups, SQS queues, and KMS encryption keys
High-availability failover benchmark report proving 100% request survival when an entire availability zone is taken offline
Anti-fake verification script terminating an active EC2 instance in AZ 1 and confirming ALB redirects 100 of 100 requests to AZ 2 in < 5 seconds

architecture.data_flow: Inbound client traffic arrives at the Application Load Balancer across multi-AZ public subnets; ALB evaluates target group health and routes requests to compute instances in private subnets; compute instances receive requests and publish asynchronous processing jobs to Amazon SQS; background workers poll SQS and process jobs; processed results and media are encrypted with AWS KMS customer managed keys and saved to Amazon S3; S3 lifecycle rules automatically move objects older than 30 days to S3 Glacier; if an entire availability zone suffers an outage, ALB detects failed targets within 5 seconds and shifts 100% of traffic to healthy AZ instances; Terraform defines the entire topology.
architecture.enforcement_mechanism: Automated ALB active health checks (`/healthz`) removing unhealthy targets from connection pools within 2 consecutive failed probes.

targets.metric: Multi-AZ Load Balancer Outage Failover Resiliency
targets.method: Percentage of requests successfully routed to secondary availability zone when primary zone is abruptly severed
targets.input: 1,000 continuous HTTP requests issued at 100 RPS while Availability Zone 1 is marked offline
targets.environment: Multi-AZ architecture deployed in LocalStack / AWS environment via Terraform
targets.minimum_pass: 1,000 of 1,000 requests succeed with 0 dropped sockets and failover rerouting in < 5.0 seconds
targets.target: 1,000 of 1,000 requests succeed with 0 dropped sockets and failover rerouting in < 2.2 seconds
targets.report: ALB failover benchmark report and target group health check event log

targets.method: Messages per second ingested into SQS queue and consumed by background workers without message loss or duplicates
targets.input: 10,000 synthetic order messages sent in burst across 10 concurrent producer threads
targets.environment: Standard SQS queue with dead-letter queue (DLQ) redrive policy enabled
targets.minimum_pass: Sustained throughput is >= 800 messages per second with 0 messages routed to DLQ
targets.target: Sustained throughput is >= 1,800 messages per second with 0 messages routed to DLQ
targets.report: SQS queue depth benchmark log and worker consumer throughput table

targets.metric: S3 Storage Cost Optimization via Automated Lifecycle Transition
targets.method: Percentage of objects older than 30 days successfully transitioned from S3 Standard to S3 Glacier tier
targets.input: 50 test objects uploaded with simulated historical creation timestamps (> 30 days old)
targets.environment: Amazon S3 bucket configured with automated lifecycle transition rules
targets.minimum_pass: 50 of 50 qualifying objects transition to GLACIER storage class with 0 data loss
targets.target: 50 of 50 qualifying objects transition to GLACIER storage class with 0 data loss
targets.report: S3 lifecycle transition audit report and storage class inventory summary

riskiest_component.name: Split-Brain Inconsistencies or Cascading Timeouts during Availability Zone Failover

riskiest_component.fallback: Automated ALB DNS shift via Route 53 health check alarms.
